newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Russia blasts NATO expansion plans at summit.
newsitem.headline: Russia blasts NATO expansion plans at summit.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, sounding a jarring note at a European security summit, told leaders from more than 50 nations on Monday that Moscow firmly opposed NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

"We have declared clearly, and declare clearly now, our firm opposition to the North Atlantic alliance's plans to move itself and its military infrastructure towards our territory," he told the Lisbon meeting of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"Is it not clear that the appearance of new dividing lines would lead to a worsening of the whole geopolitical situation in the world?"
Chernomyrdin was speaking on behalf of President Boris Yeltsin, who was unable to attend because he is still recovering after heart surgery.

He supported moves to strengthen the role of the OSCE to break down barriers in Europe, but continued the tough line against NATO enlargement which he, Yeltsin and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov have taken particularly in the past few days.
"Yes, Russia has no veto on the alliance's expansion. But nobody has a veto on our right to defend our national interests," Chernomyrdin said.

"We are convinced that there is still time and that it makes sense to think -- what can NATO expansion lead to? If our common goal is a united and peaceful Europe, then can we achieve it through the enlargement of military alliances?"
Moscow favours giving the OSCE a bigger security role and wants it to act as a counterbalance to NATO.
It says NATO enlargement to take in countries of eastern and central Europe, which were once Russia's allies in the now defunct Warsaw Pact, would threaten its security.

NATO has made clear it will not go back on its plans, and a row over expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation could overshadow the OSCE summit, just as it did the organisation's last summit in Budapest in 1994.
